solution:
**Given: **

A school has four sections i.e. A, B, C, D in Class IX.

The result of annual exams and half yearly exams for the students of these four sections is given in the table and a student is declared pass if he passes in at least one of the two examinations (half-yearly/annual)

**Calculation:**

 As Students failed in both exams is least in section C that is 23.

Students who failed half-yearly but passed in annual exams is highest in section C that is 18.

Students who passed in half-yearly but failed in annual exams is highest in section C that is 9.

Students passed both exams in section C which is 60. 

As, compared to other sections students are passed more and fail less in section C.

**Section that has the maximum pass percentage is 'section C'.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__**Section A:

Total number of students = 27 + 17 + 6 + 62 = 112

Students who passed the exam = 17 + 6 + 62 = 85

Pass percentage of section A = (85/112)×100 = 75.89%

**Section B:**

Total number of students = 25 + 15 + 8 + 57 = 105

Students who passed the exam = 15 + 8 + 57 = 80

Pass percentage of section B = (80/105)×100 = 76.19%

**Section C:**

Total number of students = 23 + 18 + 9 + 60 = 110

Students who passed the exam = 60 + 18 + 9 = 87

Pass percentage of Section C = (87/110)×100 = 79.09%

**Section D:**

Total number of students = 26 + 19 + 7 + 59 = 111

Students who passed the exam = 19 + 7+ 59 = 85

Pass percentage of section D = (85/111)×100 = 76.57%.

Section that has the maximum pass percentage is 'section C'.
